lines.en: HELLO AGAIN MY FRIEND AGAIN I BRING AGAIN A FRIEND
a friend with tongue and limbs and tongue a friend until the very end
AND EVEN IF YOU LIE INSIDE THE MOUTH THAT BUILDS YOUR WORDS
i promise that this friend is good so good he feeds the birds
NOODLE SHOP, NOODLE SHOP\nIT’S TIME FOR ONE MORE NOODLE STOP

I decide to head over to Tojo Ramen because it’s Wednesday which starts with すい which is also what watermelon starts with and watermelons remind me of Maya (old) so I need to be around food that isn’t watermelon and there is none of that nonsense here. Hello.
: Hello.
: !!! (Hello [[translated by DeepL’s new Naogmentation])
: Where’s Tsuneyo? Is it just you today?
: !... (ERROR [[Your free trial has expired])
: What are you drawing this time? I bet it’s completely normal and not at all weird.
: Oh, look. It appears that I was wrong.
: Yes. But, that aside, can I consume that bowl of noodles if you do not want to? If it just sits there collecting dust, chances are it will get all dusty.
: And nobody likes DUSTY ramen.
: If you didn’t get that, it’s because you aren’t old enough.
Nao-chan (who believes she is old enough) kicks back a passively aggressive glare that rivals the type that appears on windows when the sun is too argumentative.
She thinks for a moment about the level of sanity currently present in the protagonist today and considers whether or not she should use this to her advantage to finally sleep with him.
She doesn’t though because she’s a good girl (like thomas tongueman) and wants her first penetrative experience to be entirely consensual and also not in a ramen shop (reasonable).
She also has a problem with the narrator (me) pointing this out.
: So, I guess since Tsuneyo has taken a leave of absence to run around the top floor naked again, it’s just you and me and some dusty ramen tonight. Talk about a sooeeyowbee, am I left?
: I said “ami left?”
: Tough crowd. A kind wouldn’t even be able to wear this if you switched the d to a g.
: Is it just me or did some numbers sneak in among the punctuations there?
: (Angry silence)
(Arm emergence)
: Now, Nao! Look out now! It’s an arm emergency!
: An armergency! You should heed this arm urgency!
(I’m sorry in advance to whoever winds up translating this. And also to Tsuneyo who has to witness it from the shadowy corner since I put her in time-out.)
: Why must this always happen the moment I go on break?
(She’d be better off in a lake)
: Oh no! The mysterious arm has dragged Nao-chan into her drawing! She has finally been written out of the game! Why couldn’t it have been me?!
: Because you still have a job to do. Now put on an apron and start making gyoza. We have a catering order to knock out before my father wakes up.
: Help! The hand is me now!
: You’re wrong. The hand is all of us. For it is we who manipulate reality and not the appendigious offspring of an unlikely bloated belmach.
: Tsuneyo! Clock back in and get it off! I’ll make you as much gyoza as you want!
: I think it would be best if you just let it take you. You have an appointment on the Great Overlook. And if Nao-chan has to handle it by herself, she might expire before the fifth chapter begins.
: It tastes like belmach!
: It’s all in your head.
: What you taste is the menma.
Just like before, she was somewhere else. A room not meant for waiting, but one that she would wait for and in. Unlike a dream, but unlike not a dream too.
They called it the Great Overlook — a meeting space for those with exaggerated features who often break when viewed from the side.
In the days of yore and yolk, it would be used as a confection center. The Great British cookshow came here to make puff pastry and toss it from the ledge to feed the poles of tad.
A great frog they would make. Familiar too. He looks just like you.
Eyes open, my daughter. Appeal to the wet slabs of earthrock I have laid at your feet and confront those who seek to reshape you in images other than mine. You’ll get it in time.

(She glances to the side and realizes she is not alone. She blames him for a split second since this only happens when he is near her, but then stops doing so because she loves him for reasons that will likely never be explained outside of DLC.)
(Despite all the shakes, the man doesn’t wake. He stays on the ground while he dreams of a lake.)
: (Sleeps incestuously)
: I wouldn’t do that if I were you.
: He becomes awfully boring during moments like these. And having him awake would only detract from the real reason we’re here.
: That’s right. We’re here to see you. For each meeting with him yielded not the results needed to progress, but ones that have only prolonged the misery you face each day.
: No, Moyo. We can not eat her.
: Interesting. All this time and she still can not speak. Perhaps it’s not as much of a choice as we’ve been told.
: If you’re curious about the reasons why we’ve summoned you here, perhaps I can shine some light on it.
: Have you ever fallen down the stairs before, Nao-chan?
: No? Well, it’s kind of like that.
: You see — God is the staircase. And you’re someone who wandered into the house uninvited in an attempt to burgle and gurgle before getting caught in a mousetrap and pushed to your death.
: Now, you’re falling down the stairs and your left leg is broken and you can’t even scream for help because you’re an incomplete butterfly.
: We can fix you, though. Not us, but Us. The ones who reached through your paper and realigned your chakras. You’ve always been an amazing artist. But to think you could draw Life itself.
: Now that’s special.
: Why do you draw the things you do, Nao-chan? What are you trying to say that a mouth could not?
: If the problem truly is that you haven’t learned to use your tongue, we can give you a voice. And unlike the others, there is nothing we’d ask in return.
: We could even give you two. Then, you’d be just like Thomas.
: He’s running around in the Spectacular Playpen now. A brand new god with a throat just like yours. Would you like me to train it?
: Open your mouth.
: Now now, Moyo. Let’s not get hasty.
: This is nothing a little fish can’t handle.
: SUCK IT, YOU MYSTERIOUS GIRLWHORE! LET THE SCALES OF WISDOM REPLACE YOUR UNMOVING TONGUE WITH A TAPEWORM BONDED TO VERBALITY.
: FISH! FISH! FISH!
: How strange. Not a single hint of vibration.
: That can’t be. I think, if anything, this girl is broken.
: Which would mean that trying to change her for the better is meaningless.
: Alas. And to think we’re the only ones rooting for your success.
: Perhaps your world is doomed after all.
: Oh well. You can’t say we didn’t try.
: Well, I suppose you can’t say anything technically. But you know what I mean, I’m sure.
: And, in the event that you ever wish to truly contribute in ways much bigger than what you can fit on a sheet of paper, clap your hands thrice and wish us back.
: If your love for him is real, this is the only way you can truly help.
: Until we meet again...Nao-chan.
Seeing as the man would still not wake up, Nao-chan did what any rational girl of her age would do and crawled into his arms to take a nap.
She figured that, in the event that one of them was teleported back to earth or wherever it was they lived, they had a better chance of being teleported there together if they were touching.
And again, despite how much she wanted to be touching in a significantly more sexual manner, she was good. Like Thomas. Like menma. (I don’t like menma).
Once his arm was properly manipulated and she was snugly pressed into his chest, she closed her eyes and attempted to rid her mind of the taste of the fish of wisdom.
And she succeeded. For her heart was now racing and the fish no longer meant anything to her at all. Nothing did. Just now and Nao and now Nao and him and Him.
Him?
Which one do I mean?
The placement ruins it all.
Sleep, girl.
Dream, girl.
Be, girl.
And when you run out of things in this life that make sense, remember just how finite the amount always was.
Ignore the noise.
Be more like me.
My daughter.
My sun.
Nao’s affection has increased to [nao_love]!
